input.quote: either Party may, by written notice to the other Party, elect to initiate an arbitration proceeding pursuant to the procedures set forth in Section 13.7.3, which shall fully and finally settle the Dispute.
input.rationale: Governing law in 13.6.1 is Delaware, which sits at the accepted fallback, so we leave it alone. The dispute forum, however, is mandatory arbitration under Section 13.7.3 and Schedule 13.7.3, whose procedures (including the seat) are redacted, so no accepted court forum is designated and the seat cannot be confirmed as US-based; that fails the fallback forum element and risks walk-away territory. Section 13.6.2's service provision already presupposes "any such court" with no antecedent jurisdiction clause. We therefore target the fallback: unresolved Disputes go to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, and we conform Section 13.7.3 so the retained arbitration mechanic no longer contradicts that forum. The Section 13.7.2 carve-out for patent validity/inventorship disputes and the Section 13.11 equitable-relief carve-out are customary and left intact.

proposal.summary: Replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, consistent with the Delaware governing law already selected.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Delaware law is acceptable to us, but we need a court forum rather than arbitration, so we have made unresolved Disputes subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts and switched off the arbitration schedule. We have left the governing law, escalation and IP carve-out untouched.
